svg.data-tcam: Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM for additional table sizes
svg.data-deployment: functions standalone or as a node in a cluster from 4 Tbps up to 192 Tbps; interoperable with the rest of the S9700 series using an S9705-48D or S9725-64E as the fabric (datasheet Key Features). Keyed `deployment` rather than `role`, which is reserved for the structural role each GROUP carries
svg.data-fabric-ports: the thirteen 400G QSFP-DD ports are FABRIC ports and are for connecting to the fabric ports of an S9705-48D fabric switch only, not for service traffic (HIG Port Overview)
svg.data-breakout: service ports 0-19 can individually break out into 4x25GE or 4x10GE; if any of ports 0-19 is in breakout mode the corresponding lower-column port is disabled (HIG Port Overview). Ports 20-39 are 40GE/100GE only
svg.data-routing: full Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) support (datasheet Key Features)
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: 100GE QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4 and ZR4, up to 80 km (datasheet Compatible Transceiver Types)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: NOT STATED. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types block lists 100GE QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4 only and its Compatible Fabric Cable Types block lists 400GE QSFP-DD DAC/AEC/AOC; neither names anything for the two 10G SFP+ management ports, and the HIG's Connecting the Transceiver section names no part either. The cage takes what an SFP+ cage takes; which optics UfiSpace qualifies in it is unrecorded here rather than inferred - see the sfp-plus-optics gap
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD DAC, AEC and AOC up to 100 m - the fabric ports take cables, and the datasheet's Compatible Fabric Cable Types list carries no optical transceiver
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console, both lettered IOIOI
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A; AS/NZS CISPR 32, Class A; Anatel; NEBS GR-1089
svg.data-nebs: the Regulatory Compliance table lists NEBS GR-1089 under EMC and NEBS GR-63 under Environment; separately the datasheet's Key Benefits line reads 'Ideal for Core, Edge, and Central Office deployments (NEBS Level 3)'. Both wordings are carried because they are different claims and neither document reconciles them

circle.data-description: HIG section 10, Fan FRU LED table - Off (BMC is not up), Green (fan FRU function normal), Amber (fan FRU is abnormal, the fan speed is under 4500 rpm). Three rows and no blink states; transcribed as it stands rather than filled out from a sibling guide's longer table

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)
